title: Hooligan's Labyrinth
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Detective Boys, Agasa, Haibara) omitted by convention; the Haibara/mystery-man subplot on the platform at the end of ep280 is an unrelated running franchise thread, not connected to this murder, and is omitted for the same reason. Old cases/ep279-280_hooligans_labyrinth.json correctly identified Etsutoshi Oba as the culprit, but its backstory event (e1: 'Akano pushes Oba's twin brother down stadium stairs during a game') is imprecise: per the transcript, Akano beat the brother and threw him down the stairs *after* a match, in retaliation for a comment criticizing Akano's 'Tokyo Hooligan' blog -- not an in-game incident -- and the brother died 3 days later of a brain hemorrhage, having first lied to Oba that he'd simply fallen. The old file also omitted the actual central deduction (the seating/goal-direction contradiction in Oba's account of the match, o2's jersey provenance, and the ticket-timestamp filter that narrowed ~50 departing supporters down to 3 suspects), instead jumping straight to the physical-mark clues. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Of roughly 50 departing supporters dressed alike, only 3 held return tickets time-stamped before the match's 5 PM end -- the only way to have followed Akano onto the train without losing him -- narrowing the suspect pool to Kira, Funato, and Oba.

Oba described Hide dribbling 'right to left' and 'approaching' the goal as Naoki scored -- the view from the Spirits' side (left goal) -- yet claimed to have watched from Noir's seats on the right; the two accounts contradict.

A skin impression matching the knife's uniquely patterned scabbard was found on Oba's left forearm, opposite the watch-mark on his right arm from holding it crossed -- proof he held the concealed weapon there for a long time.

All three suspects showed posture marks consistent with standing in an overcrowded car (Kira's elbow bag-strap indent, Oba's right-arm watch mark, Funato's palm bag-grip marks), confirming presence but not distinguishing among them.
